description: This pie chart, titled “Distribution of Difficulty,” visually represents the proportion of data entries categorized by difficulty level from a dataset. The chart is divided into five distinct colored segments, each labeled with its category, percentage, and absolute count. The largest segment, colored pink, represents “Medium” difficulty, accounting for 51.8% of the total (725,892 entries). The second largest, a blue segment, corresponds to “Hard” difficulty at 25.7% (360,137 entries). Following these are “Easy” (light green, 11.2%, 157,053 entries), “Very hard” (orange, 6.5%, 91,576 entries), and “Very easy” (lavender, 4.7%, 65,332 entries). The chart includes a legend in the top-left corner that maps each color to its respective difficulty level and count, and each slice also has its percentage and count labeled directly on the chart. The segments are arranged in descending order of size, starting with “Medium” and proceeding clockwise to the smallest “Very easy” slice.
